description: Guard against regressions in scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py (SYNTHESIS row #49, P2.4 — coordination as code). The dispatcher is the deterministic coordinator-as-code contract: it resolves workflow specs (JSON or YAML) into wave-by-wave execution plans, validates the schema (no cycles, no bad refs, no missing fields), flags F8.5 fan-out overflow, and (in --execute mode) runs command-typed stages. Agent-typed stages are spec-rendered only — the lead (or /team-build) dispatches them, preserving ADR 0002's autonomy invariant (no covert L4 loops). The contract: (a) the script exists and py_compiles, (b) a valid YAML spec resolves to a plan with the expected wave structure, (c) a cycle is detected with exit 4 (the schema-error code, distinct from rc=1 command-FAIL and rc=2 INVOCATION), (d) the F8.5 fan-out warning surfaces on over-cap parallel sub-stages. If any of these regress (script deleted, validation broken, warnings silently dropped), the coordination-as-code foundation is gone and the orchestrator falls back to model-memory — exactly the failure mode the spec was written to prevent.

evals.task: Verify that scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py exists and py_compiles cleanly. A missing or syntactically-broken dispatcher breaks every spec that uses it. py_compile is the cheapest, fastest contract test we have for a Python script — no fixtures, no I/O, just byte-code generation. If this fails, the script is structurally broken before any logic runs.

context.command: python3 -m py_compile scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py && echo 'pycompile=ok' && ls -1 scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py && echo 'exists=ok'

evals.task: Verify that scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py resolves the shipped ship-merge example spec to a 4-wave, 4-stage plan. The spec has 4 top-level stages (build → validate → test → merge-agent) with a parallel sub-fan-out inside `validate`. The expected structure: 4 waves, 4 top-level stages, plan emits cleanly. The --emit-plan JSON path is the machine-readable contract a future /team-build --spec flag would consume.

context.command: python3 scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py skills/orchestrate/examples/ship-merge.yml --emit-plan | python3 -c 'import json,sys; p=json.load(sys.stdin); print("wave_count="+str(p["wave_count"])); print("stage_count="+str(p["stage_count"])); print("name="+p["name"]); assert p["wave_count"]==4, p; assert p["stage_count"]==4, p; print("all_good=1")'

evals.task: Verify that scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py exits 4 (the SCHEMA error code, distinct from rc=1 command-FAIL and rc=2 INVOCATION) when given a 2-stage cycle. Cycle detection is load-bearing: without it, the dispatcher would silently loop on a malformed spec and the lead would never know. The 5 exit codes are: 0=PASS/PLAN, 1=command-stage FAIL, 2=bad invocation, 3=parse error, 4=schema error (cycle/bad ref/missing field). The fixture writes the cycle spec to /tmp, runs the dispatcher, asserts the rc.
evals.fixed_by: P2.4 (validate_spec uses Kahn's algorithm for cycle detection)

evals.task: Verify that scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py surfaces the F8.5 fan-out warning when a parallel stage has more sub-stages than the cap (default 5). The warning is critical: the lead must split over-cap parallels into chunks of 5 BEFORE dispatch, otherwise the audit goes wrong (the original 2026-06-12 failure was a soft-cap prompt that overshot to 44 agents). The warning goes on the human plan (stdout) AND on the --emit-plan JSON output. The fixture writes a 17-sub-stage parallel, runs the dispatcher at the default cap (5), asserts the warning text is in the output.

context.command:
printf 'name: overflow-test
stages:
  - id: validate
    type: parallel
    stages:
' > /tmp/overflow-test.yml && for i in $(seq -w 1 17); do printf '      - {id: s%s, type: command, command: "true"}
' "$i" >> /tmp/overflow-test.yml; done && python3 scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py /tmp/overflow-test.yml 2>&1 | grep -E 'F8.5 OVERFLOW|has 17 sub-stages' | head -3

evals.task: Verify that scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py surfaces the F8.4 under-parallelized advisory when a parallel stage has fewer than the F8 floor (3) of AGENT sub-stages. Symmetric counterpart to the F8.5 overflow warning (the min 3 / max 5 band, owner request 2026-06-16). ADVISORY only — the dispatcher flags but never blocks — and scoped to agent fan-out (a 2-command parallel like lint+typecheck must NOT fire it). The fixture writes a 2-agent parallel, runs the dispatcher at the default floor (3), and asserts the advisory text is in the output.

context.command:
printf 'name: under-test
stages:
  - id: fan
    type: parallel
    stages:
      - {id: a, type: agent, agent_type: claude, prompt: x}
      - {id: b, type: agent, agent_type: claude, prompt: y}
' > /tmp/under-test.yml && python3 scripts/orchestrate-dispatch.py /tmp/under-test.yml 2>&1 | grep -E 'F8.4 UNDER|under-parallelized' | head -3

evals.fixed_by: 0.2.12 (build_plan emits f8_4_under_warnings; min-per-wave default 3, owner request)
